newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline falls amid talk of imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline falls amid talk of imports.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale gasoline prices fell late Thursday, as imports headed for the region amid growing output from refineries, traders said.

CARB unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was assessed at 74.50 cents a gallon, down 1.50 cents from yesterday. The grade has fallen 12 cents, or 14 percent, from last Wednesday, when fears of a refinery strike inflated the market.
The rally, which lifted CARB gasoline prices to 86.5 cents on March 25, drew the imports that are now threatening to flood the market.
"It's four or five cargoes coming in," from the U.S. Gulf and Far East, one broker said.
Meanwhile, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported that gasoline stocks in PADD 5 (West Coast) rose 98,000 barrels last week.
Traders said conventional gas in L.A. shed one cent from late Wednesday, with traders offering shipments at 68 cents and no buyers seen.
CARB diesel fell 1.50 cents TO 77/78 in line with L.A. gasoline, with low sulphur grade was unchanged at 67/68 cents.
Jet fuel bucked the downturn by rising a half cent on rumors of production problems in San Francisco. A source familiar with the refinery denied the trade rumor.
Energy futures traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange pared yesterday's steep losses, with May crude futures settling unchanged and gasoline up 0.29 cents to 60.90 cents.
